title: Framing Algorithmic Recourse for Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: The task is to present counterfactuals deemed normal by an anomaly detection model, enabling explanations or recommended countermeasures for anomalous tabular instances with discrete feature values.

gap.claim: Algorithmic recourse for anomaly detection on tabular data with only discrete feature values is identified as unexplored.

contributions.claim: CARAT is an approach for context-preserving algorithmic recourse for anomalies in tabular data that is described as effective, scalable, and agnostic to the underlying anomaly detection model.

CARAT uses a transformer encoder-decoder to explain anomalies by identifying features with low likelihood and generates semantically coherent counterfactuals by modifying those features using the anomalous instance context.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments demonstrate CARAT's efficacy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Algorithmic recourse has been explored for supervised machine learning models to support interpretable, transparent, and robust outcomes.
Recourse for anomaly detection, particularly discrete-valued tabular data, is identified as unexplored.
The goal is to provide normal counterfactuals for explaining anomalies or recommending countermeasures.
CARAT identifies low-likelihood features with a transformer encoder-decoder and modifies them using instance context to generate semantically coherent counterfactuals.
The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating efficacy.

source_observation.claim: The method identifies low-likelihood features and modifies them while using the overall context of the anomalous instance to generate counterfactuals.

interpretation.claim: Explanatory recourse can combine anomaly localization with context-aware counterfactual generation.

application.claim: For discrete tabular anomaly explanations, first locate unlikely features and then generate changes constrained by the instance's feature context.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond tabular data with discrete feature values.

unknowns: The supplied abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
The supplied abstract does not describe the counterfactual-generation constraints or implementation details beyond the transformer encoder-decoder and contextual feature modification.
